subject: cardboardRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.

spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A grinning six-year-old in a homemade cardboard-box robot costume: a taped corrugated torso box with a marker-and-bottle-cap control panel, a box helmet with a face window and foil antennae, paper-tube arms ending in cardboard pincer claws, and foil-strapped shins over sneakers.
spec.layout: Front is +Z, the kid's left is +X, the model is centred on x = 0, and z runs from about -0.32 (backpack) to +0.26 (panel dials and toes). The kid is about 1.15 m tall and stands in a neutral T-pose with the arms out sideways, 5 degrees down, and the legs shoulder-width apart. From the floor up: white sneakers (y 0 to 0.08), blue leggings with cardboard shin and knee guards (y 0.08 to 0.50), and the TORSO BOX (x +-0.25, y 0.50 to 0.95, z +-0.18), which is open at the bottom so the legs come out of its hem. The HELMET BOX (x +-0.19, y 0.95 to 1.30, z +-0.19) sits on top of the torso box. A rectangular FACE WINDOW is cut in its front (x +-0.115, y 1.04 to 1.21), and the kid's round head with a big grin shows through it. Antennae (foil straws with caps and a spring) rise to y 1.42, and toilet-roll ear tubes stick out of the sides at x +-0.19 to +-0.26. The arms leave round holes in the torso sides at (+-0.25, 0.85) as paper-towel-tube sleeves with a segmented dryer-hose elbow, foil-wrapped forearms and a two-jaw cardboard pincer claw at x +-0.72 to +-0.86, open like a crab. The chest has a hand-built control panel with dials, bottle-cap buttons and glowing LEDs, and the back has a smaller cardboard backpack box with tubes and a foil vent. CARDBOARD CRAFT STYLE: every big surface is a plain box in brown corrugated tones, with thin darker edge strips and a few lighter or darker ridge lines for the corrugation. Packing-tape strips (lighter tan, slightly proud of the surface) cover seams and corners. Details are black marker lines, scribbles and hand-drawn shapes made of thin dark parts seated on the cardboard, painted accents in poster red, blue, yellow and green, crinkled low-poly foil (faceted, 6 to 8 sides), hot-glue blobs, and slightly wonky craft proportions (small 1 to 3 degree tilts on added pieces, never on the main boxes). Only LEDs, the claw eye-lights and the panel screen glow.

parts.builds: Both legs, mirrored, and the sneakers. Thighs and shins are thin tapered tubes in leggings blue (thigh radius about 0.06, knee 0.05, shin 0.045), bent with the hip, knee and ankle joints. Darker leggings knee patches sit on the front of each knee, and a few small marker-doodle stars and dashes in white and yellow on the thighs read as the kid's own drawings. Each shin has a cardboard shin guard: a thin curved box in cardboard with cardboardDark edge strips and corrugation ridges, held by two foil strips (foil) wrapped round the leg and tied with small tape tabs. A little red-painted stripe and a marker 'bolt' doodle sit on the guard. The upper thigh disappears inside the torso hem at y 0.50, and a thin cardboardInner shadow collar can show where the legs meet the box. The sneakers are chunky low-poly white shoes about 0.09 wide and 0.24 long, from z -0.04 to 0.20, with a toe cap bump, a sole slab in sole colour with a dark tread line, two red velcro straps or a lace row of small white bars with red aglets, a red heel tab and a small red side stripe. Soles rest on y = 0, sunk at most 0.002.
parts.attaches: Top of each thigh enters the torso hem at mounts legTopL and legTopR (y 0.50, x +-0.09) and rides hipL/hipR, kneeL/kneeR, ankleL/ankleR and toeL/toeR. The torso part owns the hem; nothing here extends above y 0.52.

parts.builds: The main costume box, the bare cardboard shell, with no panel hardware. It is a box of x +-0.25, y 0.50 to 0.95, z +-0.18, in cardboard, built from a hollow-looking shell: thin walls with a cardboardInner rim at the open bottom hem (y 0.50) and a dark opening where the legs enter. Corrugated edges show as thin cardboardDark strips on all vertical corners and the hem, with a few shallow ridge lines (thin boxes in cardboardLight and cardboardDark) running across the front, back and sides. Packing-tape strips (tape colour, 0.01 proud) cover the vertical corner seams and run in an 'X' pattern over a patched corner on the back. The top has four folded flaps that frame the neck hole: front and back flaps lean outward at about 20 degrees and the side flaps are folded in, showing cardboardInner undersides and tape tabs. Two round arm holes in the side faces at (+-0.25, 0.85) have a marker-outlined ring and a cardboardInner collar of radius about 0.065. Over the shoulders go two shoulder-strap loops (tape and a tapeBrown string) that go up over the top flaps. A tapeBrown shipping-label rectangle with marker lines on the lower left side, a stamped 'THIS SIDE UP' arrow, a red 'FRAGILE' sticker, a few hot-glue blobs and some scuff patches in cardboardDark on the corners. Inside the neck hole, a dark ring shows the kid's blue-shirt collar (leggings colour). Everything sits on the box faces; the front face z = 0.18 is left clear in the centre rectangle x +-0.16, y 0.60 to 0.86 for the gadget panel.
parts.attaches: Sits on legs at the hem (torsoBase) and under the helmet at torsoTop / helmetBase. Arm holes at armHoleL and armHoleR; the arms start inside them. The chest panel mounts on torsoFrontFace and the backpack on torsoBackFace; both are built by the gadgets part.

parts.builds: All the craft hardware on the torso, built outside the torso volume only. FRONT: a control panel board of cardboardDark (about 0.32 wide, 0.24 tall, 0.02 thick, z 0.18 to 0.20) with a tape border, centred on chestPanelCenter. On it: a row of three round dials made of bottle caps (red, blue, yellow) with marker tick marks and a small needle bar each; a big central 'screen' of a black marker-framed rectangle with a glowCyan inner pane and a marker zigzag line; two rows of 4 small bottle-cap buttons (green, yellow, red, blue) with marker rings; a pull-switch made from a clothespin and a tapeBrown string; three round LEDs in glowRed, glowLime and glowCyan (glowing); a hand-drawn marker speaker grille of six thin parallel bars; a drawn heart or a smiley, a bolt-and-gear emblem and a 'B-07' style label made from thin marker bars, all seated on the board. SIDES: a rectangular foil-patched vent flap on each side below the arm hole at y 0.62. BACK: a backpack box (about 0.34 wide, 0.34 tall, 0.12 deep, z -0.30 to -0.18, centred on backpackCenter) in cardboardLight with tape corners and a lid flap, two foil-wrapped tubes (radius 0.03) bent up and over the top like exhaust pipes with foilDark rings, a round foil dish or vent, a red painted 'ON/OFF' switch, a dangling curly cord (swept thin coil in marker) and two tapeBrown backpack straps that reach the shoulders over the top flaps. Small hot-glue blobs, tape tabs and marker scribbles on the back finish it.
parts.attaches: Panel back face sits flush on torsoFrontFace (z 0.18) at chestPanelCenter. Backpack front face sits flush on torsoBackFace (z -0.18) at backpackCenter. Side vents sit on x = +-0.25. Rides chest and spine joints. Nothing may block the arm holes at armHoleL/R (radius 0.07) or the neck hole.

parts.builds: The kid's head and the cardboard helmet box. KID: a round, slightly chubby head (radius about 0.10, centred on kidHeadCenter) in skin, a short neck in skinShade, ears, a small nose, rosy cheeks (mouth colour, subtle), two big eyes (white sphere, iris-coloured iris, black pupil, a tiny white highlight) set at x +-0.045, a thick brow pair in hair colour, and a wide open grin. The mouth is a separate lower jaw (rides the jaw joint) and an upper jaw/lip, with a mouth-colour interior, two small white teeth rows and a small tongue. Hair in hair colour: a solid cap plus a modest number of overlapping tufts and a fringe that sticks out above the eyes. HELMET: a box of x +-0.19, y 0.95 to 1.30, z +-0.19 in cardboard, built as thin walls with a cardboardInner rim round a rectangular face window (x +-0.115, y 1.04 to 1.21 on the front), with thick marker outline round the window and tape strips on corners and seams. A hinged cardboard visor flap above the window (rides visor joint) tilted slightly up, with a foil strip and a red stripe. Corrugated edge strips on every corner, ridge lines, tape X over the back seam, a marker mouth-grille pattern of five bars on the front chin area under the window, two drawn marker 'eyebrow' bars above and a red-painted 'B' on the forehead. EARS: toilet-paper-roll tubes (radius 0.05, length 0.07) on the sides at earTubeL and earTubeR, painted red on the left and blue on the right, with foil end caps and a marker spiral. ANTENNAE: two foil-wrapped straws (radius 0.008) from antennaBase at x +-0.07 leaning outward 12 degrees to y 1.42, one topped by a yellow bottle-cap disc and one by a red pom-pom sphere, and a small coil spring (thin swept spiral in foilDark) on one. A little foil dish on the very top centre. Hot-glue blobs where the antennae and ears attach.
parts.attaches: Neck base and helmet base sit on the torso top at neckBase / helmetBase (y 0.95); the helmet's bottom rests on the torso top flaps. The kid's head rides head and jaw; the helmet rides head; the visor flap rides visor; the neck rides neck. The face window faces +Z at faceWindowCenter.

parts.builds: Both arms, mirrored (left is +X), from the arm holes out to the claw tips. UPPER ARM: a paper-towel tube (radius 0.055) from x +-0.23 (inside the hole) to x +-0.45, in cardboardLight with a spiral-seam line in cardboardDark, two painted stripe bands (yellow and red), and a tape collar at the shoulder end. ELBOW: a segmented dryer-hose joint, five stacked thin rings or a ribbed tube (radius 0.05) in foilDark with foil highlights between x +-0.45 and +-0.50 around elbowL/R. FOREARM: a foil-wrapped tube (radius 0.05, low-poly crinkled faceting, 6 to 8 sides) to x +-0.68 with tape cuffs at both ends, three little rivet bottle-cap buttons in blue, and a marker 'wristwatch' band. HAND: a cardboard pincer claw, a palm block (box about 0.06 wide) at x +-0.69 to +-0.73 with tape, and two jaws made from flat extruded cardboard shapes (curved crab-claw outlines with a cardboardDark edge, a foil tip, and serrated marker 'teeth' ticks): the top jaw rides clawTop*1 and clawTop*2 and the bottom jaw rides clawBot*1 and clawBot*2, open in a V with tips near x +-0.86 and about 0.08 apart in y. A tiny glowLime LED sits on the back of each palm. Small hot-glue blobs and tape tabs at each join. Kid's skin shows only in a small gap at the wrist cuff (a skinShade ring).
parts.attaches: Starts inside the torso arm holes at armHoleL/armHoleR (x +-0.25, y 0.85); the collar sits flush against the box wall at x = +-0.25. Rides shoulder*, elbow*, wrist* and the claw* joints. Nothing is built for |x| < 0.23.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a spec for a child in a cardboard-box robot costume, humanoid with a skeleton. I'm sizing the kid at about 1.15 m tall, with the box torso around 0.5 m wide and the arms spread through the sides so the overall width comes to roughly 1.2 m.

I'm working out the body proportions now: the kid's legs run from the floor up to the hips, with the box torso covering the middle section. The box helmet sits on top of the head, and I'm checking where it lands relative to the head height so the total size comes out right, with antennas adding a bit more on top.

I'm now placing the torso box, about 0.5 m wide and running from the hips up to just under the shoulders, with arm holes cut at shoulder height on each side. The arms are cardboard tubes that extend sideways, with foil over the upper section and a glove or claw mitt at each end, and I'm checking their lengths against the kid's arm span.

I'm settling the arm geometry now: shoulders at about 0.29 m out from center, with the arms angled slightly downward to a total width near 1.7 m. Then I'm turning to depth, working out how far the torso and feet extend forward and back, and whether a cardboard backpack with tubes would fit behind.

I'm now deciding how to split the parts list: the legs, shoes, and hip joints as one group, and the torso box with its flaps, control panel, buttons, and backpack straps as another.

I'm settling the parts list now, going with five pieces: legs, the main torso box, a chest panel and backpack for the decorations, the head with its helmet and antennas, and the arms with their tube sleeves and mitts.

I'm laying out the budget for each part and then the skeleton joints, starting with the hips at the base of the spine and working up through the chest, neck, and head.

I'm now sizing the helmet: a box about 0.36 m on each side, centered a little above the head, with a face window cut in the front so the kid's face shows through.

I'm finishing the vertical layout: the torso box runs from 0.50 to 0.95 m, and the helmet sits on top from 0.95 to 1.30 m, with the head's center around 1.12 m. Next I'm placing the hip joints on either side of center for the legs.

I'm working out where the torso box's bottom edge and the legs meet, with the leg joints at the hips and the sneakers at the floor, and I'm deciding to keep the cardboard shin guards strapped over the leggings.

I'm weighing how to lay out the arms: shoulders at about 0.25 m out from center, elbows and wrists tapering outward, with the hands ending near 0.85 m. I'm still deciding whether the forearms should be foil-wrapped cardboard tubes with the kid's bare hands showing, or whether the hands should be cardboard claws instead.

I'm settling on a pincer-style claw for each hand instead of plain fingers, with a top and bottom jaw on each side, which suits the robot look.

Now I'm listing the skeleton joints for the spec, working down the spine from the hips through the chest, neck, and head, and placing the jaw hinge slightly forward of the head joint.

I'm adding the visor as a hinge on the helmet, then moving on to the leg joints: the left hip sits at about x 0.09 with the knee and ankle chained below it.

I'm placing the ankle and toe joints for each leg, then moving on to the arms: shoulders at about 0.25 m out from center, elbows and wrists tapering outward, with the claw digits defined as pincers at the wrist.

I'm finishing the arm geometry now: the claw jaws on each hand open vertically, with a top and bottom pincer that angle outward, and the arms reach to about 0.86 m from center on each side. I'm checking that total width against the target and deciding the palette is fine as it is.

I'm listing the color palette now, with cardboard tones, tape, foil, paint colors, glow accents, and skin and hair shades for the kid.

I'm trimming the palette now, dropping the cheek color so the list fits under the twenty-four-color limit.

I'm now defining the color palette, trimming it to exactly 24 entries with the cardboard, tape, foil, paint, glow, and skin tones, and I'm dropping the sneaker accent and eye white in favor of simpler shared colors. Next I'm placing the hip pivot and the front hem point where the torso box meets the legs.

I'm placing the remaining reference points for the torso and head, the shoulder holes, leg tops, and antenna base. Then I'm working out which part owns the torso box and which owns the chest panel.

I'm now sorting out the torso box's details: the arm rims at the side faces, the shoulder straps, and the corrugation and scuff marks. Separately, the gadgets part gets the chest panel, dials, LEDs, backpack, and side vents, with the panel sitting on the torso's front face.

I'm sizing the helmet as a box about 0.38 m wide, running from 0.95 to 1.30 m, with a face window cut at the front. I'm placing the kid's eyes and head center so the window lines up with the face, and I'm keeping the helmet's axes straight so the rig stays simple.

I'm specifying the antennas as two foil-wrapped straws capped with bottle caps or pom balls, one of them spring-mounted, plus a pair of red and blue toilet-paper-roll ear tubes at the sides of the helmet. I'm also setting the hands as folded, foil-covered cardboard claws, with the forearms as foil-wrapped tubes with tape cuffs and the upper arms as paper-towel-roll tubes.

I'm now sizing the legs: the thighs are about 0.06 m in radius, the shins 0.045, and the hips sit a little inside the torso hem. I'm also adding the leggings with knee patches, cardboard shin guards with a foil strip, and sneakers with laces, a sole, and a velcro strap.

I'm checking the leg boxes and the torso box's bounds, and I'm weighing whether the top flaps should stick up a little past the torso's top edge to fold around the neck.

I'm now sorting out the torso box's shell bounds and checking how the gadgets box overlaps it, so the parts only build the outside volume.

I'm going over the backpack and the overall depth, which runs from about -0.32 to 0.26 on z, and I'm settling the head box bounds, including the ear tubes and antennas reaching up to 1.42.

I'm sizing the bounding boxes for the arms and the whole body, with the arm boxes covering the outer sides and a shoulder stub reaching in from the torso. I'm also checking the claw heights so the tips stay within the overall bounds.

I'm now writing out the joint list explicitly, starting with the hips at the root and working up the spine through the chest and neck, with the hip joints named left and right for each leg.

I'm listing the joints for the spec now, placing the jaw pivot near the head joint and the visor as a hinge on the helmet front. I'm also defining the claw joints at the wrist, with the top and bottom pincers angled outward from the hand.

I'm finishing the joint list now, listing the tip positions for the claw digits and noting that the right side mirrors the left with the x sign and direction flipped. Then I'm grouping everything into the five parts and tallying the count: seven spine and head joints, eight leg joints, and seven arm joints.

Writing out the mirrored right-side joints now, with the x signs and directions flipped from the left.

I'm checking the right arm's claw joints against the wrist height, confirming the claws sit around 0.80 and the mirrored offsets line up. I'll also mount the remaining pieces to the rig.

Still writing the arm helpers, going with a cylinder aligned along X using the part's `dir` option.

Still working through the arm geometry, figuring out how to place the tubes along their actual direction between two points.

Still working out the spiral's center and axis, then starting the claw outline on the arm's x-direction.

Still writing the claw outline for the top jaw, working out the points that shape its curve and where the tip sits relative to the bottom one.

Still writing the claw outline, working out the jaw's curve and placing its tip with the bottom one.

Still writing the claw outline, checking the top jaw's thickness and tip so it doesn't collapse into a thin sliver.

Still writing the claw outline, now working out the teeth along the inner edge of the top jaw.

Still working on the teeth along the top jaw's inner edge, placing small dark boxes that poke slightly below the edge.

Still writing the claw, adding the foil tip as a small cone on the tip joint and weighing whether the dark cardboard edge should be a slightly thicker extrude sitting behind the jaw.

Still writing the claw, now working out a dark strip along the outer edge and how to orient a thin box along the segment.

Still writing the claw, now adding a rounded rim along the top jaw's outer edge so the thin piece reads as solid.

Still writing the claw, now placing the palm box and a tape wrap around it, with a glowing LED on top. Next I'm adding the wrist cuff as a shaded ring with tape bands on either side.

Still writing the claw, now adding the foil crinkle and rivets on the forearm, plus a watch band and face near the wrist.

Still writing the arm, now placing the upper arm tube with its yellow and red bands and a tape collar, and adding a dark cardboard edge ring at the far end.

Still working on the arm's upper section, setting the height at each point along its length so the tube and its bands follow the curve.

Still working on the arm's shape, with the rings following the slope of the tube segment they sit on, and the seam spiral's axis tilted slightly downward.

Still writing the spiral, working out its starting point and whether the sweep radius matches the arm's cross-section, then settling on a detail setting for the path.

Still writing the jaw outline, working through the points that shape the top jaw's curve.

Still writing the jaw, working out the outline's bottom edge and mirroring it for the bottom jaw around its center height.

Still working on the jaw's teeth along the top jaw's inner edge, placing small dark boxes just below the edge line.

Still writing the claw's foil tip, placing a small cone at the jaw's tip, angled outward along the arm.

Adding two small glowing spheres on the palm's front as eyes, then setting up the random foil shards on the forearm.

Still working on the foil crinkles: placing small dark shards on the forearm with random small rotations, and a faint off-white hot-glue tint for the blobs.

I'm going to write one function that builds the head and helmet, keeping it fairly detailed but efficient. I'll use b.part with mostly three geometries to keep it low-risk, and I'm working out how the Ctx type comes into the function signature, since it's supposed to come from the module.

Still working through the head and helmet geometry, with the joint positions and the face window dimensions laid out.

Still writing the jaw and mouth details, with the lower jaw sphere and the dark mouth cavity placed at the front of the head.

Still writing the jaw and face details, with the chin, lower lip, and a curved grin that I'll build from a few sweeps. Next up are the eyes, nose, and cheeks, and I'm starting to work out where the ears go.

Still writing the hair, a top cap sphere tilted slightly back with fringe tufts over the forehead.

Still writing the helmet walls, with the cardboard shell, window rim, and edge strips going around the front, sides, and top.

Still working out the helmet details: the eyebrow bars sit just above the window, and the red B on the forehead needs to fit in the strip between the window and the top edge. The visor flap is the tricky part, since it projects forward over the same forehead area and I'll need to tilt it so it doesn't collide with the B.

I'm working out the visor flap: a thin box hinged at the top of the window, tilted about ten degrees so its front edge lifts up, and the red B sits on the forehead above the window, clear of it. The eyebrow bars go just above the window on either side. The flap parts will go on the visor joint, with a foil strip and a red stripe along the top.

Still writing the ear tubes, sized to sit on the helmet sides, with a foil cap at each end and a spiral marker band wrapped around them.

Still writing the antennae and their tips, with the yellow cap and red pom-pom, and I'm weighing whether to add a coiled spring on one of the rods.

Still writing the antennae, now adding a coil around the red pom-pom rod and a foil dish with hot-glue blobs at the bases.

Still writing the helper function for the helmet boxes, with a rotation option and the head bone as the default.

Still adding the helmet's edge details: tape strips along the front and side corners, and a thin tape seam running across the top.

Still writing the helmet's side ridges and back wall lines, placing the thin strips around the ear-tube area so they don't collide with it.

Still writing the front wall pieces: a bottom and top strip across the front, plus narrow side strips flanking the window.

Still writing the cardboard frame, with the inner rim strips around the window and the thicker outline bars just outside it.

Still sizing the helmet walls: the front and back are full width, the side walls sit just inside them, and the top plate covers everything. Height of the sides is trimmed so they stop under the top.

Still sizing the top wall so its edges don't z-fight with the front piece's top face.

Still sizing the top wall and side walls so their faces don't overlap in a way that z-fights, with the top plate lifted just above the front pieces. Next up is the hair.

Still working on the jaw, sizing a lower-jaw sphere and placing it just under the head so the grin has a shape to sit on.

Still sizing the jaw, with a slightly flattened lower hemisphere that bulges just below the head to form the chin, and now working out a dark mouth recess placed on the head's front surface at grin height.

Still sketching the mouth, with a dark recess set just proud of the head surface and a curved grin built from a few sweep points.

Still working on the mouth: a dark interior recess, white upper and lower teeth, a pink tongue, and a curved lower lip, all sitting on the jaw group.

Still working out the eye placement: they sit just proud of the head surface at the front, with a small radius. I'm also setting the visor hinge and the tilted flap, plus the foil and red stripe on it. For the hair, I'm placing fringe cones over the forehead and giving the cap a partial hemisphere so it doesn't cover the eyes.

Still placing the brow boxes just above the eyes, aligned to the head surface.

Still placing the fringe tufts over the forehead, angling them forward and slightly downward so they sit clear of the brows.

Still placing the marker bars: a tall vertical stroke set slightly left of center, with top, middle, and bottom bars across the front for the B's bowl, plus the right-side bumps.

Still placing the eyebrow marker bars and the neck cylinder, then I'll write out the final code with the helper and bone variables.
